pages.text: A grain of radius r in water is struck by molecules from every side and wanders: its mean square displacement grows as ⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt, with D = kT/(6πηr) (Einstein). Measure D and you have Boltzmann's constant, and from it Avogadro's number. The water's viscosity η falls steeply as it warms. n tracks measure ⟨x²⟩ to √(2/n); each position is found to about a tenth of the objective's resolution, 0.61λ/NA, and that error adds to the wandering.
$(thing)Set$(): Frame interval t, Tracks followed, Numerical aperture.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Convection in the cell: the drift biases the tracks by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The water in the cell has frozen; The water in the cell is boiling.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Fewer tracks and shorter intervals are faster.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Water viscosity: η = A·10^(B/(T − C))$(br)Diffusion coefficient: D = kT/(6πηr)$(br)Mean square displacement: ⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt$(br)Resolution: δ = 0.61λ/NA$(br)Position error: 2σ²/⟨x²⟩$(br)Statistical error: √(2/n)$(br)Error in Avogadro's number: all added in quadrature
